title: Zero-EUV array: one grating mask plus spacer cascade
idea: Constraint: no EUV anywhere in the array. Print a single ~80 nm-pitch ArF-immersion grating per direction and derive active, buried wordline, bitline and storage-node contacts by self-aligned spacer quadrupling with tone inversion at the crossings, leaving only two relaxed-pitch cut masks at the array edge.
why: Fact 4: removes the 5-7 EUV exposures and ~60% of array masks; est. -25-35% wafer cost and no dependence on the single EUV supplier.

title: Laser interference lithography exposes the periodic cell lattice maskless
idea: Constraint: no litho tool may cost over $5M. A DRAM array is a perfect lattice, so expose it with 193 nm immersion four-beam interference that writes 40 nm-pitch hexagonal hole or line lattices over the full field in one flash; a conventional dry-ArF mask exposure only trims the non-periodic array edges and periphery.
why: Fact 4 capital: interference tools ~$3-5M vs $200M+ for EUV, >150 wafers/hour, no reticles for array layers; litho cost per array layer -80%.

title: Statistical capacitors: unaligned anodic-alumina pores caught by oversized pads
idea: Constraint: no lithography and no plasma etch for the capacitor mold. Anodize a deposited aluminum film into self-ordered ~30 nm-pitch pores (AR >100 for free), deliberately unaligned to the cells; each oversized landing pad catches 3-5 pores, pores straddling gaps are sealed by a selective ALD cap, and the per-cell capacitance spread is trimmed out at test.
why: Facts 1 and 4: swaps the hardest high-AR cryo-etch and its mask for a wet bath; AR 100-200 gives ~1.5x Cs; capacitor-module capex -60-70%.

title: Metal-assisted wet etching carves 150:1 buried trench capacitors
idea: Constraint: no high-AR plasma etcher in the fab. A patterned Pt catalyst mesh sinks into single-crystal silicon in HF/H2O2 (MacEtch), carving 150:1 trenches at room temperature on a wet bench; the catalyst is stripped and reclaimed and the trenches become buried capacitors under the access transistors.
why: Facts 1 and 4: AR 150 in crystalline silicon gives ~10 fF cells; a ~$2M wet bench replaces an $8-10M etcher; the top surface is freed for wiring.

title: Crystal planes, not lithography, define atomically flat vertical channels
idea: Constraint: nothing finer than 80 nm may be printed for the active area. On (110) wafers, anisotropic TMAH etching exposes vertical {111} walls, so coarse 80 nm lines are wet-thinned to 8-10 nm fins whose sidewalls are crystal planes, then cut into pillars for vertical-channel access transistors.
why: Facts 3 and 4: removes EUV/SAQP from active definition; near-zero line-edge roughness tightens the leakage tail ~2x; the wet etch costs a few dollars per wafer.

title: Superlattice edge stamps print 16 nm wordlines without optics
idea: Constraint: pitch must come from deposition thickness, never from light. Grow a Si/SiGe superlattice of 8 nm layers, cleave and selectively recess its edge into a ridge master, metallize the ridge tips and transfer them as wordline/bitline gratings (superlattice nanowire pattern transfer), each master printing thousands of wafers through daughter stamps.
why: Fact 4: sub-20 nm pitch set by epitaxy with zero scanner time; critical-layer litho capital -50-80%.

title: Frozen cell: decade-long nanoimprint templates replace node chasing
idea: Constraint: one cell geometry for ten years. Pattern every array layer by jet-and-flash nanoimprint from e-beam masters replicated into hundreds of daughter templates; R&D money shifts to stacking, periphery and sensing while array litho cost collapses to template wear.
why: Fact 4: a node buys only 10-20% cost per bit; freezing it avoids ~$1-2B of litho reinvestment per node and cuts array litho cost ~80%.

title: Five-mask array wafer: sense amps live on bonded logic wafer
idea: Constraint: the array wafer gets five masks (active, wordline, bitline, capacitor, bond pad). Sense amplifiers, decoders and all upper metal sit on a separately made CMOS wafer hybrid-bonded face-to-face, with a 16:1 local bitline-select device formed in the same wordline step so bond pitch can stay near 0.5 um.
why: Fact 7: the ~49% periphery moves to a cheap logic node and stops occupying DRAM-process area; array wafer cost -50%, array die density ~1.8x.

title: Doping-superlattice 3D DRAM: porosify p+ layers instead of SiGe
idea: Constraint: no SiGe epitaxy, because strain caps the tier count. Grow fast all-silicon epi with alternating p+/p- doping, then electrochemically porosify only the p+ layers from the vertical-bitline slit to open lateral cavities for capacitors and gates, allowing 100+ tiers without strain relaxation.
why: Fact 2: clears the ~26-tier break-even with high-rate Si epi (~3x throughput vs Si/SiGe) and no misfit dislocations; cost per tier falls.

title: Scanner-hour exchange: rent idle logic-fab EUV for DRAM layers
idea: Constraint: the DRAM fab may buy zero EUV scanners. A brokered exchange sells logic foundries' EUV utilization dips; DRAM lots travel in sealed FOUPs to a nearby logic fab for 2-3 critical exposures under a standardized resist/track recipe, then return.
why: Fact 4 capital: avoids $400M+ of scanners per DRAM fab, lifts industry EUV utilization 10-15%, and makes U.S. DRAM fabs viable next to Arizona/Texas logic fabs.

title: ISO-6 ballroom fab survives on 4,096 self-repairing tiles per die
idea: Constraint: a cleanroom one to two classes dirtier than today. Wafers stay only in sealed minienvironments, and each die is 4,096 independently testable 1 Mb tiles with 20% spares and a boot-time self-test controller that remaps dead tiles, tolerating ~10x defect density.
why: Capital and time: fab shell/HVAC is ~20-25% of fab capex; halving it and cutting build time ~1 year helps U.S. manufacturability while spares hold yield.

title: Unsawn wafer as memory module: no dicing, packaging or DIMMs
idea: Constraint: zero back-end line. Ship the whole 300 mm DRAM wafer as a ~1.5 TB memory slab: a wafer-level redistribution layer stitches good dies into a mesh, bad dies are fenced off, edge SerDes expose CXL ports and a cold plate bonds to the back.
why: Test, packaging and module assembly are ~15-25% of DRAM cost; removing them while using every good die gives ~20% lower cost per bit and a rack-scale product.

title: Display-fab memory: stacked oxide-TFT DRAM on Gen-8.5 glass
idea: Constraint: no silicon wafers at all. Repurpose idle Gen-8.5 LCD/OLED backplane lines to build 1T1C capacity memory at ~1 um rules on 5.5 m2 glass, about 100 GB per TFT tier and 8 stacked tiers per panel, sliced into CXL capacity modules with ~200 ns access.
why: Glass area costs ~100x less than silicon and the capex is stranded and depreciated; target <$2/GB capacity tier with zero crucible quartz and no EUV.

title: Helium-free fab: hydrogen-neon chuck cooling and hydrogen-tracer leak checks
idea: Constraint: zero helium deliveries. Switch electrostatic-chuck backside cooling in high-AR etch and deposition from He to H2/Ne blends with redesigned micro-groove chucks that restore gas conductance, replace He leak testing with 5% H2/N2 tracer sniffers, and membrane-recapture any legacy He.
why: Removes exposure to the Qatar helium outage (~30% of supply) that can idle etch-heavy DRAM lines; mainly supply-risk removal, ~1-2% gas cost saving.

title: Crucible-free wafers: epitaxial lift-off from reusable seed wafers
idea: Constraint: no new high-purity quartz crucibles. Grow 20 um device-grade epi on a double-porous-silicon release layer, bond it to a polysilicon or SiC-ceramic handle, split it off, re-polish the seed and reuse it 20-50 times.
why: Scarce resource: cuts Czochralski crystal (and Spruce Pine crucible) demand >90%; wafer cost -30-50% at volume; epi reactors are U.S.-buildable.

title: Area-selective deposition grows landing pads where masks once went
idea: Constraint: delete three masks. Inhibitor monolayers that bind only to dielectric let ALD grow storage-node landing pads and bitline contact plugs only on exposed TiN/Si, self-aligned to the buried geometry, with a short etch-back to clear stray nodules.
why: Fact 4: eliminates the overlay-critical landing-pad EUV layer and two contact masks, ~5-8% of wafer cost and one fewer EUV pass.

title: Supercritical CO2 drying lets capacitors grow taller without support meshes
idea: Constraint: cut ultrapure water use 80%. Replace post-etch wet cleans and spin-dry with supercritical CO2 plus co-solvent cleaning; with zero surface tension, 100:1 capacitor pillars no longer collapse, so the support-lattice (MESH) films and their masks can be dropped.
why: Facts 1 and 4: removes 1-2 masks and lets AR rise from ~70 to ~100 (+40% Cs); fab water -80%.

title: Rotary spatial ALD deposits capacitor dielectrics at 300 wafers per hour
idea: Constraint: one-tenth of today's deposition tool count. Wafers orbit under separated precursor and purge zones near atmospheric pressure, so ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 stacks grow by motion rather than valve cycling; long-dwell and ozone-assisted sectors restore conformality in 70:1 holes.
why: ALD is a growing slice of capex, especially for 3D DRAM's dozens of ALD steps; ~10x throughput per tool, ~-70% module capex.

title: Open DRAM PDK lets idle U.S. foundries run memory lots
idea: Constraint: no access to incumbent DRAM IP. A public consortium develops and releases a royalty-free 1T1C process kit (recipes, cell, sense amp, redundancy) at a 20-28 nm class on standard logic toolsets, qualified at several U.S. foundries so spare capacity can produce DRAM.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital: activates depreciated fabs with ~zero new fab capex and breaks the three-company know-how wall.

title: Multi-beam e-beam writes only cuts, making DRAM variants maskless
idea: Constraint: no new mask set per product. Print array gratings once with cheap periodic litho, then use a ~250k-beam electron writer only on sparse cut and via layers (<5% exposed area) to customize die size, ECC layout and bank count.
why: Mask sets cost $10-20M; cut-only exposure makes e-beam throughput viable (~10-20 wph) for specialty and low-volume DRAM lines.

title: Tungsten-free buried wordline: fully silicided polysilicon fill
idea: Constraint: zero tungsten. Fill the buried-wordline trench with doped polysilicon over the gate oxide, cap it with thin nickel or cobalt and anneal until the whole fill converts to NiSi/CoSi2 (full silicidation), then recess; no WF6 CVD and no TiN barrier.
why: Removes China-concentrated tungsten (~80%) and WF6 tools from the cell; fewer fill/CMP steps and the freed barrier volume lowers wordline resistance.

title: Block copolymer quadruples a sparse capacitor-hole lattice
idea: Constraint: print only one in four capacitor holes. Sparse ArF guide posts at twice the pitch template a cylinder-forming block copolymer by graphoepitaxy, which self-assembles the missing hexagonal holes at ~24 nm pitch; the minority cores are removed and transferred into the mold.
why: Fact 4: replaces EUV or SAQP for the densest hole layer; 4x density multiplication from a cheap mask, about one fewer EUV layer.

title: Prefab cleanroom pods add DRAM capacity in $500M steps
idea: Constraint: capital may arrive only in $500M increments. Factory-built cleanroom pods, each a complete array-only line for ~2k wafer starts/month, are shipped and plugged into shared utilities and a partner logic fab for periphery, going from order to output in ~12 months.
why: Capital intensity and time: replaces $15B, 3-5-year lumpy bets with demand-matched modules, lowering financing risk and speeding a U.S. ramp.

title: Idle U.S. silicon-carbide power fabs build hot-proof DRAM transistors
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: 4H-SiC's 3.26 eV bandgap keeps off-state leakage negligible even hot, so build the access transistor (or gain-cell write device) in 200 mm SiC power fabs left underused by the SiC glut, then hybrid-bond a silicon capacitor/periphery wafer on top.
why: Fact 3 and capital: retention of seconds or more at 125 C (refresh ~1000x rarer) using existing U.S. SiC capacity instead of new DRAM fabs; density is limited by ~90 nm SiC litho.

title: Mist-CVD gallium oxide write transistors, deposited without vacuum
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years and with no vacuum deposition tools: grow alpha-Ga2O3 (~4.9 eV bandgap) channels by ultrasonic mist CVD at atmospheric pressure and ~400 C over the CMOS periphery, giving a gain-cell write transistor whose projected leakage stays in the sub-aA range even hot.
why: Fact 3: refresh-free retention at 125 C; capital: mist-CVD tools cost ~1/10 of ALD/PVD clusters and are BEOL-compatible.

title: Hot wafer-sort at 150 C replaces package burn-in ovens
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: test retention on 150 C hot chucks at wafer sort to map each die's leakage tail, fuse weak rows into redundancy and burn a per-bank temperature-refresh table into eFuses, so no packaged burn-in is needed and every shipped die is pre-screened 25 C beyond its rating.
why: Back-end capital: removes burn-in boards, ovens and ~48 h cycles (~3-5% of cost) while guaranteeing the 125 C retention tail.

title: Glass-lid wafer-level package: hermetic, polymer-free, sealed before dicing
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years with zero polymers: direct-bond a borosilicate lid wafer carrying through-glass vias onto the finished DRAM wafer at low temperature, forming a hermetic chip-scale package before dicing with solder-free Cu pillar outputs.
why: Packaging capital and reliability: removes molding, underfill and organic-substrate steps (~-30% package cost) and the humidity/ionic failure modes that dominate at 125 C.

title: Subtractively etched ruthenium wiring: no copper damascene, no barriers
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: deposit blanket Ru, plasma-etch it into lines and gap-fill with dielectric, skipping trench etch, barrier/seed, plating and Cu CMP; ruthenium's high melting point gives ~10x electromigration headroom at 125 C and nothing can diffuse into the cells.
why: Facet: drops ~4 tool types per metal level (plating, barrier PVD, Cu CMP, anneal); interconnect cost -20% with long-life EM margin.

title: ABF-free ceramic package substrates sidestep the build-up film chokepoint
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: replace organic ABF build-up substrates (one dominant film supplier) with low-temperature co-fired glass-ceramic substrates and silver-sinter die attach, whose expansion matches silicon and which do not absorb moisture or creep at 125 C.
why: Scarce resource and U.S. manufacturability: LTCC lines are mature and domestic; removes an organic-substrate chokepoint and solder fatigue at high temperature.

title: Pre-patterned back-gate SOI wafers give temperature-tracking threshold voltage
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: the substrate supplier delivers SOI wafers with a buried back-gate grid under a thin BOX, so planar fully depleted access transistors raise their threshold by back bias as the die heats, holding 125 C leakage at 85 C levels while the fab skips its buried-wordline trench module.
why: Facts 3 and 4: moves ~10 front-end steps to a relaxed-pitch substrate process; leakage tail at 125 C cut ~10x by bias.

title: Antiferroelectric zirconia capacitors store more charge using existing tools
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: tune the ZrO2 already used in DRAM capacitors into a dopant-stabilized antiferroelectric phase with asymmetric electrodes, so the built-in bias parks the cell on the steep field-induced transition and the effective k in the sensing window exceeds ~100 from -40 to 125 C.
why: Facts 1 and 4: same ALD and etch tools, but ~2x charge per area lets capacitor AR fall from ~70 to ~40, cutting etch time and hardmask steps.

title: Inductive coil links stack DRAM dies without any TSVs
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: stacked dies thinned to <20 um talk through on-chip spiral coils and receive power through heavily doped silicon columns, so there are no TSV etch/fill/reveal steps, no microbumps and no metallurgical joints to grow intermetallics over a decade at 125 C.
why: Fact 6: removes the TSV area and yield tax (~3x area per bit, -20-30% yield) and several back-end tool types.

title: Backside-etched trench capacitors use the wafer itself as mold
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: after front-end transistors are bonded to a carrier, thin the wafer to ~3 um and etch capacitor trenches from the back into the silicon under each access transistor, using crystalline silicon as the mold (no carbon mold, no support mesh) for ~25 fF cells.
why: Facts 1 and 3: 4-5x Cs buys 125 C retention; front-side contact AR collapses and the capacitor mold and support-lattice deposition steps disappear.

title: Transistorless cross-point capacitors: two line masks per stacked tier
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: replace the access MOSFET with a two-terminal wide-gap punch-through selector (AlN/SiC heterojunction) whose barrier keeps hot leakage tiny, giving a 4F2 one-selector-one-capacitor cross-point that needs only two line/space masks per tier and stacks monolithically.
why: Facts 2 and 4: 4F2 per tier and ~2 masks per tier vs ~25; cost per bit could fall several-fold if the selector holds fA-class leakage at 125 C.

title: Single-crystal tiers by repeated low-temperature layer transfer
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: polysilicon tiers leak too much hot, so each 3D tier is a 50 nm crystalline Si film split from a donor by hydrogen implant and bonded below 400 C, with laser dopant activation; the donor is reused, and each tier costs one bond plus ~3 masks.
why: Fact 2: crystalline channels keep the 125 C leakage tail of planar DRAM while stacking; no epi superlattice and no single 100:1 etch.

title: Hydrogen-sink liners stabilize oxide-semiconductor cells at 125 C
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: a same-chamber ALD sandwich of AlOx barrier plus Ti/TiOx absorber islands traps hydrogen that would otherwise diffuse into the oxide channel and turn it conductive, so standard hydrogen-rich SiN passivation and forming-gas anneals stay in the flow.
why: Fact 3 and capital: keeps BEOL oxide-channel memory stable for a decade at 125 C without special hydrogen-free tools or materials.

title: In-die reliability sensors finish qualification in weeks, not quarters
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: embed TDDB, BTI, EM and retention monitor arrays in every die and calibrate a physics-of-failure model at 175 C, replacing lot-by-lot 1000-hour high-temperature operating life tests with continuous, data-driven qualification.
why: Capital and time: cuts 4-6 months from each new fab or node ramp, so capital earns revenue sooner while proving the 10-year life.

title: Inverted fin capacitor: storage discs between continuous plate sheets
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: deposit a ~20-layer stack of continuous plate metal sheets alternating with sacrificial layers, etch one hole per cell, laterally recess the sacrificial layers into rings and fill dielectric plus storage metal, giving a stack of storage discs interleaved with the plates.
why: Facts 1 and 4: ~3-6 fF at AR ~15 instead of 70, so the extra charge for 125 C retention comes from deposition, not from the hardest etch.

title: Fluorine-free molybdenum wordlines grown barrier-less from chloride precursors
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: deposit Mo from MoO2Cl2 directly on the wordline gate oxide with no TiN barrier and no fluorine, so there is no fluorine to attack the oxide, and the freed barrier volume goes to a thicker, longer-lived gate dielectric.
why: Tungsten chokepoint removed; better time-dependent breakdown at 125 C; resistance ~-30% at buried-wordline dimensions.

title: Droplet self-alignment bonds dies at 10,000 per hour
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: water droplets on hydrophilic pads pull dies into sub-0.5 um alignment by capillary force, then oxide-oxide and Cu-Cu direct bonds form in a ~250 C anneal, with no polymer and no solder to age at 125 C.
why: Facts 6 and 4: ~10x die-to-wafer throughput vs ~$5M precision pick-and-place bonders; stacked-memory back-end capex down several-fold.

title: Sacrificial-polymer air gaps between bitlines, no extra mask
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: fill bitline gaps with a thermally decomposable polymer, cap it with porous SiCN and bake at ~400 C so it evaporates through the cap, leaving rigid air gaps that stay stable at 125 C.
why: Facts 1 and 3: bitline capacitance -30-40% raises sense signal, so the Cs needed for hot retention needs ~30% less capacitor height and no added mask.

title: Rutile TiO2 on RuO2 doubles k and halves capacitor etch
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: grow Al-doped rutile TiO2 (k ~80-100), templated below 400 C by RuO2 electrodes whose high work function plus Al doping suppress hot Schottky leakage, so capacitor aspect ratio drops from ~70 to ~35.
why: Facts 1 and 4: single-step capacitor etch, thinner carbon hardmask, fewer support layers; capacitor module cost ~-30%.

title: Implant-free junctions from in-situ doped selective epitaxy
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: replace cell and periphery junction implants with in-situ doped selective epitaxy and conformal plasma doping, eliminating end-of-range implant damage that seeds trap-assisted gate-induced drain leakage at 125 C.
why: Facts 3 and 4: leakage tail tightened ~3x hot; removes ~6 implant steps and their masks and fewer high-current implanters.

title: Self-limiting oxidation thins channels until quantum confinement widens bandgap
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: oxidize silicon pillars where stress makes oxidation stop at a ~2 nm core, so quantum confinement lifts the effective bandgap to ~1.6-2 eV; the final channel size is set by chemistry, not lithography.
why: Fact 3: hot leakage ~100x lower; fact 4: removes a critical trim litho/etch step; variability is the main risk.

title: Revive IBM-heritage deep-trench eDRAM as hot-rated standalone memory
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: license the existing SOI deep-trench eDRAM process (~25-40 fF cells) held by a U.S. foundry and productize it as standalone 125 C DRAM in its New York fabs, with no new tool or process development.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital: large-Cs trenches meet hot retention immediately, near-zero new capex, months not years to first product.

title: Automotive-first entry: new U.S. fab bootstraps on 125 C premium
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: a new entrant builds a small 10-20k wafer/month fab tuned for the 125 C automotive and industrial grade that incumbents underserve, selling at 2-3x commodity prices to profit at low volume, then learns its way into commodity DRAM.
why: Capital intensity: lowers break-even scale and investor risk for a U.S. DRAM entrant; grows domestic know-how before the commodity fight.
